summary: Two 11-story office towers at 1655 & 1725 3rd St (combined ~584,000-586,200 sq ft, sources differ on the exact figure), LEED v4 Gold per Office Snapshots, developed by a joint venture of Alexandria Real Estate Equities (10%), Uber Technologies (45%) and the Golden State Warriors (45%), with SHoP Architects credited as architect by ArchDaily, completed in 2021 per SF Standard. Uber and the Warriors each lease office space at the property for their headquarters (The Real Deal, 2025); in 2023 Uber marketed all of 1725 3rd St for sublease and said that building was unoccupied (SF Standard).

milestones.text: Both towers complete construction (SF Standard: the four-building campus was initially completed during the pandemic in 2021; Office Snapshots lists a 2021 completion date)

SF Standard reports that Uber is marketing the entirety of 1725 Third St for sublease and that the building was never occupied by Uber; an Uber spokesperson says one of its four Mission Bay buildings is currently unoccupied

facts.value: Joint venture (Event Center Office Partners) of the Golden State Warriors (45%), Uber Technologies (45%) and Alexandria Real Estate Equities (10%)

SHoP Architects, per ArchDaily's 'Uber Headquarters' project page (its listed area, 423,000 ft2, differs from these two towers' combined size); interiors of Buildings 3 and 4 by Huntsman Architectural Group (Office Snapshots)
~584,000 (Office Snapshots) to ~586,200 (The Real Deal, 2025) combined; 'more than 586,000' (CommercialCafe, 2020); sources disagree on the exact figure
LEED v4 Gold (also WELL), per Office Snapshots

Uber Technologies and the Golden State Warriors each lease office space at the property for their headquarters (The Real Deal, 2025). In May 2023 Uber marketed all of 1725 Third St for sublease and said that building was unoccupied; the marketing materials cite 73 parking spaces for that building; Uber's 2022 blog post (as quoted by SF Standard) said more than 3,500 employees would be based at its four-building headquarters.

open_questions: 2026-09-23: this record's geometry was migrated off status.csv (record_id changed from the blklot '8722063' to 'mission_bay_uber_3_4') because DataSF's own Assessor Parcel dataset gives this parcel and the neighboring Chase Center arena byte-identical geometry (one shared master-condo superblock parcel). The new geometry is the union of both towers' own real OpenStreetMap building footprints (OSM ways 1410182008 and 1410183655) instead -- see the geojson's own digitization_method.

Uber's SEC EDGAR company record lists 1725 3rd Street as its business address (read 2026-09-29), though a May 2023 SF Standard report said that specific building had never been occupied by Uber and was being marketed for sublease -- current occupancy is genuinely unclear and not resolved here.

This project's own DataSF business-registration data shows several Uber-internal registrations here (Bon Appetit @ Uber cafeteria service across multiple floors, Uber Freight Holding Corporation, a Mercedes-Benz-branded garage/showroom) not otherwise researched or added as facts in this pass.
No dedicated primary source (an Alexandria or Uber press release specifically) was found for the exact completion date of each tower individually; 2021 is used as a combined year.

2026-09-23 pass: searched for a total development or construction cost for the two towers. Press coverage only turns up financing and lease figures -- Uber's $136,000,000 payment for a 45% joint-venture stake, its $1,000,000,000 in lease payments over 20 years, and the $600,000,000 CMBS refinancing already cited above -- none of which is a stated construction or development cost, so none is recorded here.

2026-09-29 accuracy audit: the 'January 2022 occupancy', '20-year lease', '~4,000 employees' and '145 parking spaces' claims were removed because no readable source states them (Office Snapshots has no lease or headcount; SF Standard cites Uber's 2022 blog for 'more than 3,500 employees' across four buildings and says 1725 3rd St was never occupied). The ArchDaily page credits SHoP Architects but lists 423,000 ft2 and a 2022 year, so which buildings it covers is not confirmed. Completion is dated 2021 (SF Standard, Office Snapshots); no month is sourced.
